# package canbus

```go
import "github.com/otfabric/go-canbus"
```

Package canbus is the transport-neutral core of go-canbus: CAN and CAN FD frames, identifiers, data length codes, filters, error frames, the [Transport](#type-transport) interface and the [Bus](#type-bus), which shares one transport among many subscribers.

Transports live in subpackages: socketcan (Linux SocketCAN raw sockets) and virtual (a deterministic in-memory bus for tests and simulation). Higher layers build on a Bus: isotp (ISO 15765-2), capture (candump, JSON Lines and pcap traces, replay), and candb with dbc, kcd and codegen (message and signal databases).

A CAN identifier names a message, not a device: nothing in this module infers which physical node sent a frame.

## Variables

```go
var (
	// ErrClosed reports an operation on a bus, subscription or transport
	// that was closed.
	ErrClosed = errors.New("canbus: closed")

	// ErrTimeout reports an operation that did not complete in time. A
	// context deadline is reported as the context's error instead.
	ErrTimeout = errors.New("canbus: timeout")

	// ErrInvalidFrame reports a frame that cannot be represented or sent:
	// see [Frame.Validate]. A *[FrameError] carries the detail.
	ErrInvalidFrame = errors.New("canbus: invalid frame")

	// ErrUnsupported reports an operation or frame type the transport
	// does not support: SocketCAN on a system other than Linux, a CAN FD
	// frame on a socket not opened for CAN FD, a kernel filter on a
	// virtual port.
	ErrUnsupported = errors.New("canbus: unsupported")

	// ErrQueueFull reports a frame that could not be queued because a
	// bounded queue was full and its policy is to reject.
	ErrQueueFull = errors.New("canbus: queue full")

	// ErrInvalidOption reports an option value a bus, transport or
	// connection cannot be constructed with.
	ErrInvalidOption = errors.New("canbus: invalid option")

	// ErrInterfaceDown reports an interface that is down or does not
	// exist.
	ErrInterfaceDown = errors.New("canbus: interface down")

	// ErrBufferOverflow reports frames lost because a receive buffer
	// overflowed (the kernel's socket queue, a transmit queue that is
	// full: ENOBUFS).
	ErrBufferOverflow = errors.New("canbus: buffer overflow")
)
```

Sentinel errors. They are usually wrapped with detail; test with errors.Is.

## Functions

### func DLCToLen

```go
func DLCToLen(dlc uint8, fd bool) int
```

DLCToLen returns the payload length of a data length code (only its low 4 bits are used). fd selects the CAN FD table: codes 9..15 mean 12, 16, 20, 24, 32, 48 and 64 bytes. For classical CAN they all mean 8 bytes.

### func IsXLText

```go
func IsXLText(s string) bool
```

IsXLText reports whether s looks like a CAN XL frame in can-utils notation (a CAN XL header after the first "#"), as opposed to a classical or CAN FD frame.

### func KernelID

```go
func KernelID(fr *Frame) uint32
```

KernelID returns the Linux can\_id of a frame: the identifier with CAN\_EFF\_FLAG, CAN\_RTR\_FLAG and CAN\_ERR\_FLAG.

### func LenToDLC

```go
func LenToDLC(n int) uint8
```

LenToDLC returns the smallest data length code whose CAN FD length holds n bytes: 0..8 map to themselves, 9..12 to 9, ..., 49..64 to 15. Lengths above 64 return 15.

### func PadFD

```go
func PadFD(data []byte, pad byte) []byte
```

PadFD returns data padded with pad to the next valid CAN FD length. data is returned unchanged when its length is already valid.

### func RoundUpFDLen

```go
func RoundUpFDLen(n int) int
```

RoundUpFDLen returns the smallest valid CAN FD length of at least n bytes, or 64 when n exceeds 64.

### func ValidFDLen

```go
func ValidFDLen(n int) bool
```

ValidFDLen reports whether n is a payload length a CAN FD frame can carry: 0..8, 12, 16, 20, 24, 32, 48 or 64.

### func XLKernelID

```go
func XLKernelID(x *XLFrame) uint32
```

XLKernelID returns the identifier Linux's CAN\_RAW\_FILTER matches for a CAN XL frame: the priority with the VCID in bits 16..23, without any flag (a standard data frame identifier).

## Types

### type Bus

```go
type Bus struct {

	// t, when it carries CAN XL

	// metrics, when it observes CAN XL

	// closed when the reader has stopped

	// copy on write
	// why the reader stopped

	// WithStartOnSubscribe

}
```

Bus shares one [Transport](#type-transport) between many users. A single reader goroutine receives every frame and hands a copy to each [Subscription](#type-subscription) whose filters it passes; Send may be called from any goroutine.

The Bus owns the transport: Close closes it. Subscriptions can be added and closed at any time, also while frames arrive. A frame read while no subscription exists reaches nobody: to receive from the first frame on, create the bus with [WithStartOnSubscribe](#func-withstartonsubscribe).

On an [XLTransport](#type-xltransport) the bus also carries CAN XL frames: [Bus.SendXL](#func-bus-sendxl) sends them and subscriptions opened [WithXL](#func-withxl) receive them.

#### func NewBus

```go
func NewBus(t Transport, opts ...Option) (*Bus, error)
```

NewBus starts a bus on t. The reader goroutine starts at once and keeps draining the transport even while there are no subscriptions, so that a transport's own receive queue does not overflow.

#### func (Bus) Close

```go
func (b *Bus) Close() error
```

Close stops the reader, closes every subscription and the transport. It waits for the reader to stop and is safe to call more than once.

#### func (Bus) Done

```go
func (b *Bus) Done() <-chan struct{}
```

Done returns a channel closed when the bus reader has stopped.

#### func (Bus) Err

```go
func (b *Bus) Err() error
```

Err returns why the reader stopped: nil while it runs, ErrClosed after Close, or the transport error that ended it.

#### func (Bus) Name


Name returns the interface name of the bus, possibly "".

#### func (Bus) Send


Send validates the frame and transmits it. It is safe for concurrent use.


SendXL validates a CAN XL frame and transmits it. It fails with ErrUnsupported when the transport does not carry CAN XL (is not an [XLTransport](#type-xltransport)). It is safe for concurrent use.

#### func (Bus) State


#### func (Bus) Stats


Stats returns the bus counters.

#### func (Bus) Subscribe

```go

```

Subscribe adds a subscription. It returns ErrClosed when the bus is closed.

#### func (Bus) Transport

```go

```

Transport returns the transport of the bus. Do not call its Receive: the bus reader does.

### type ErrorClass

```go
type ErrorClass uint32
```

ErrorClass is the class bit set of an error frame: the identifier of a frame with FlagError, with the values of Linux's can/error.h. It is also the mask that selects which error frames a socket receives.

```go
const (
	ErrClassTxTimeout       ErrorClass = 0x001 // TX timeout (by netdevice driver)
	ErrClassLostArbitration ErrorClass = 0x002 // lost arbitration; bit in Data[0]
	ErrClassController      ErrorClass = 0x004 // controller problems; Data[1]
	ErrClassProtocol        ErrorClass = 0x008 // protocol violation; Data[2], Data[3]
	ErrClassTransceiver     ErrorClass = 0x010 // transceiver status; Data[4]
	ErrClassNoAck           ErrorClass = 0x020 // no acknowledgement on transmission
	ErrClassBusOff          ErrorClass = 0x040 // bus off
	ErrClassBusError        ErrorClass = 0x080 // bus error (may flood)
	ErrClassRestarted       ErrorClass = 0x100 // controller restarted
	ErrClassCounters        ErrorClass = 0x200 // TX/RX error counters in Data[6], Data[7]

	// ErrClassAll selects every error class.
	ErrClassAll ErrorClass = 0x1FFFFFFF
)
```

Error classes.

#### func (ErrorClass) String

```go
func (c ErrorClass) String() string
```

String lists the classes, for example "controller|bus-off".

```go
type ErrorInfo struct {
	Class ErrorClass
	// ArbitrationBit is the bit in which arbitration was lost (0 =

	// Controller is the controller status, for ErrClassController.

	// Protocol and ProtocolLocation describe a protocol violation, for

	// TxErrors and RxErrors are the error counters, valid when

	TxErrors, RxErrors uint8
	CountersValid      bool
}
```

### type Filter

```go
type Filter struct {
	ID     ID
	Mask   ID
	Format Format
	Remote RemoteMatch
	Invert bool
}
```

Filter selects frames by identifier: a frame matches when (frameID & Mask) == (ID & Mask), restricted by Format and Remote, and negated by Invert.

The semantics are those of Linux's CAN\_RAW\_FILTER: [Filter.Kernel](#func-filter-kernel) returns the can\_filter the kernel would be given, and the software matcher evaluates exactly that expression on the kernel's flag-encoded identifier. In particular, with FormatAny a mask of 0x7FF also matches extended identifiers whose low 11 bits agree, as in the kernel.


ExactExtended returns a filter for one 29-bit identifier.

```go

```

ExactStandard returns a filter for one 11-bit identifier.

#### func ParseFilter

```go
func ParseFilter(s string) (Filter, error)
```

ParseFilter parses the notation of [Filter.String](#func-filter-string) and candump's: "\<id>:\<mask>" or "\<id>~\<mask>" (inverted), hexadecimal; an identifier of more than 3 digits selects extended identifiers. Suffixes ",std", ",ext", ",any", ",data" and ",rtr" set Format and Remote explicitly.

#### func (Filter) Kernel

```go

```

Kernel returns the Linux can\_filter values (can\_id, can\_mask) of f.

#### func (Filter) Match

```go
func (f Filter) Match(fr *Frame) bool
```

Match reports whether a data or remote frame passes the filter. Error frames are selected by an error mask instead; Match reports false for them.

#### func (Filter) MatchXL

```go
func (f Filter) MatchXL(x *XLFrame) bool
```

MatchXL reports whether a CAN XL frame passes the filter, as the kernel decides it: on [XLKernelID](#func-xlkernelid), so a filter for a standard identifier selects the CAN XL frames of that priority (and any VCID unless the mask covers bits 16..23), and a filter for an extended identifier selects none.

#### func (Filter) String

```go
func (f Filter) String() string
```

String formats the filter as candump does: "123:7FF", "12345678:1FFFFFFF" for extended (with an 8-digit identifier), "123~7FF" when inverted, with ",std" / ",any" / ",data" / ",rtr" for what candump's notation cannot spell. [ParseFilter](#func-parsefilter) reads it back unchanged.

### type FilterSet

```go
type FilterSet struct {
	Filters   []Filter
	Join      bool
	ErrorMask ErrorClass
}
```

FilterSet is a list of filters with the combination rule of CAN\_RAW\_FILTER: a frame passes when it matches any filter, or, with Join (CAN\_RAW\_JOIN\_FILTERS), all of them. An empty set passes every data and remote frame. ErrorMask selects the error frames that pass (CAN\_RAW\_ERR\_FILTER); zero passes none.

#### func (FilterSet) Match

```go
func (s *FilterSet) Match(fr *Frame) bool
```

Match reports whether the frame passes the set.

#### func (FilterSet) MatchXL

```go
func (s *FilterSet) MatchXL(x *XLFrame) bool
```

MatchXL reports whether a CAN XL frame passes the set ([Filter.MatchXL](#func-filter-matchxl)).

Filterer is implemented by transports that filter in the kernel, in hardware or as frames arrive. Frames that do not pass are never delivered to Receive.

### type Frame

```go
type Frame struct {
	// ID is the identifier without flag bits. For error frames it holds
	// the Linux error class bits (CAN_ERR_*).
	ID ID
	// Flags holds the format bits.
	Flags Flags
	// Len is the payload length in bytes: 0..8 for classical frames, one
	// of 0..8, 12, 16, 20, 24, 32, 48, 64 for CAN FD frames. For remote
	// frames it is the requested data length (the DLC), and no data is
	// carried.
	Len uint8
	// Len8DLC preserves a classical frame's raw DLC of 9..15, which also
	// means 8 data bytes. It is 0 otherwise.
	Len8DLC uint8
	// Data is the payload; only the first Len bytes are meaningful.
	Data [MaxFDLen]byte
	// Timestamp is the receive time reported by the transport (the
	// kernel's for SocketCAN), or the zero time.
	Timestamp time.Time
	// Interface names the interface the frame was received on, if known.
	Interface string
	// Echo reports that the frame is the receiving socket's own
	// transmission, delivered back because receive-own-messages is on.
	Echo bool
}
```

Frame is one CAN or CAN FD frame with its receive metadata.

The payload is a fixed array so that a Frame is a plain value: sending and receiving frames does not allocate. Bytes of Data beyond Len are zero in frames produced by this module. Use [Frame.Payload](#func-frame-payload) for the valid bytes.

#### func (Frame) Validate

```go
func (f *Frame) Validate() error
```

Validate checks that the frame can be transmitted or represented: the identifier fits its format, the length is valid for the frame type, the flags are consistent (no remote CAN FD frame, no BRS/ESI without FD, Len8DLC only with Len 8) and the bytes beyond Len are zero. Error frames are only checked for their length. The returned error is a \*[FrameError](#type-frameerror) wrapping ErrInvalidFrame.

### type ID

```go
type ID uint32
```

ID is a CAN identifier without flag bits: 11 bits for a standard frame, 29 bits for an extended frame. Whether an identifier is standard or extended is recorded in [Frame.Flags](#func-frame-flags), not in the ID, because 0x123 as a standard and as an extended identifier are different identifiers on the bus.

```go
const (
	MaxStandardID ID = 0x7FF      // largest 11-bit identifier
	MaxExtendedID ID = 0x1FFFFFFF // largest 29-bit identifier
)
```

Identifier ranges.

### type Metrics

```go
type Metrics interface {
	// OnFrameSent is called after a frame was handed to the transport.
	OnFrameSent(iface string, f *Frame)
	// OnFrameReceived is called for every frame read from the transport,
	// before filtering by subscriptions.
	OnFrameReceived(iface string, f *Frame)
	// OnDrop is called when n frames were lost.
	OnDrop(iface string, reason DropReason, n uint64)
	// OnError is called when a send or receive failed.
	OnError(iface, op string, err error)
	// OnQueue is called after a frame was queued for a subscription with
	// the queue's depth and capacity.
	OnQueue(iface string, depth, capacity int)
	// OnStateChange is called when the bus state changes.
	OnStateChange(iface string, from, to State)
}
```

Metrics is an optional callback interface for observing a [Bus](#type-bus). A nil Metrics disables collection.

The methods are called synchronously, possibly from several goroutines at once; implementations must be safe for concurrent use and must not block. Frames passed to them must not be retained or modified. Embed [NopMetrics](#type-nopmetrics) to implement only some callbacks and to stay compatible when methods are added.

#### func WithStartOnSubscribe

```go
func WithStartOnSubscribe() Option
```

WithStartOnSubscribe defers the bus's reader until the first [Bus.Subscribe](#func-bus-subscribe) (or [Bus.Close](#func-bus-close)). Until then frames wait in the transport (a SocketCAN socket's receive buffer), so the first subscription sees them all; without this option the reader starts in NewBus and frames that arrive before the first subscription are lost. Error state ([Bus.State](#func-bus-state)) is tracked once the reader runs.

### type Overflow

```go
type Overflow uint8
```

Overflow is the policy of a subscription whose queue is full.

```go
const (
	// DropNewest discards the frame that does not fit (the default). The
	// reader never waits for a slow subscriber.
	DropNewest Overflow = iota
	// DropOldest discards the oldest queued frame to make room.
	DropOldest
	// Block makes the bus reader wait until the subscriber takes the
	// frame. A slow subscriber then delays every other subscription and
	// lets the transport's own queue overflow instead: use it only when
	// losing frames in this process is worse.
	Block
)
```

Overflow policies.

### type ProtocolViolation

```go
type ProtocolViolation uint8
```

ProtocolViolation is Data\[2] of a protocol error frame.

```go
const (
	ProtBit      ProtocolViolation = 0x01 // single bit error
	ProtForm     ProtocolViolation = 0x02 // frame format error
	ProtStuff    ProtocolViolation = 0x04 // bit stuffing error
	ProtBit0     ProtocolViolation = 0x08 // unable to send dominant bit
	ProtBit1     ProtocolViolation = 0x10 // unable to send recessive bit
	ProtOverload ProtocolViolation = 0x20 // bus overload
	ProtActive   ProtocolViolation = 0x40 // active error announcement
	ProtTx       ProtocolViolation = 0x80 // error occurred on transmission
)
```

Protocol violation types.

#### func (ProtocolViolation) String

```go
func (p ProtocolViolation) String() string
```

String lists the violation bits.

### type RemoteMatch

```go
type RemoteMatch uint8
```

RemoteMatch selects data or remote frames in a [Filter](#type-filter).

```go
const (
	RemoteAny      RemoteMatch = iota // data and remote frames
	RemoteDataOnly                    // data frames only
	RemoteOnly                        // remote frames only
)
```

Remote frame selection.

### type State

```go
type State uint8
```

State is the state of a bus as far as the library can tell: whether it runs, and the controller's error state reported by error frames.

```go
const (
	StateUnknown State = iota
	StateActive        // running; controller error active (or no report)
	StateWarning       // error warning (an error counter reached 96)
	StatePassive       // error passive (an error counter reached 128)
	StateBusOff        // bus off
	StateDown          // the interface is down
	StateClosed        // closed by the application
)
```

Bus states.

#### func (State) String

```go
func (s State) String() string
```

String names the state.

### type Stats

```go
type Stats struct {
	TxFrames  uint64 // frames sent
	TxBytes   uint64 // payload bytes sent
	RxFrames  uint64 // frames received
	RxBytes   uint64 // payload bytes received
	RxErrors  uint64 // error frames received
	Dropped   uint64 // frames lost: kernel receive queue overflow, full subscription queues, injected faults
	TxErrors  uint64 // failed send attempts
	RxFailure uint64 // failed receive attempts other than cancellation
}
```

Stats are frame counters of a transport or bus.

### type Statser

```go
type Statser interface {
	Stats() Stats
}
```

Statser is implemented by transports that keep counters.

### type SubscribeOption

```go
type SubscribeOption func(*Subscription)
```

SubscribeOption configures a [Subscription](#type-subscription).

#### func WithFilters

```go
func WithFilters(fs FilterSet) SubscribeOption
```

WithFilters selects the frames the subscription receives. Without it, every data and remote frame is received and no error frame.

#### func WithOverflow

```go
func WithOverflow(o Overflow) SubscribeOption
```

WithOverflow sets the policy when the queue is full (default DropNewest).

#### func WithQueueSize

```go
func WithQueueSize(n int) SubscribeOption
```

WithQueueSize sets the queue capacity (default DefaultQueueSize).

#### func WithXL

```go
func WithXL() SubscribeOption
```

WithXL makes the subscription receive CAN XL frames too: CAN, CAN FD and CAN XL frames share its queue in arrival order and are read with [Subscription.ReceiveAny](#func-subscription-receiveany) ([Subscription.Receive](#func-subscription-receive) and [Subscription.ReceiveXL](#func-subscription-receivexl) skip the other kind; [Subscription.Frames](#func-subscription-frames) is nil). The subscription's filters select CAN XL frames as Linux's CAN\_RAW\_FILTER does ([FilterSet.MatchXL](#func-filterset-matchxl)). Without it, CAN XL frames are not delivered, as to a SocketCAN socket without CAN\_RAW\_XL\_FRAMES.

#### func WithoutEcho

```go
func WithoutEcho() SubscribeOption
```

WithoutEcho drops frames the transport marks as this socket's own transmissions ([Frame.Echo](#func-frame-echo)).

### type Subscription

```go
type Subscription struct {

	// without WithXL
	// WithXL: every kind, in arrival order

}
```

Subscription receives the frames of a [Bus](#type-bus) that pass its filters, through a bounded queue. Its receive methods and Frames may be used from one goroutine at a time; Close and the counters from any.

#### func (Subscription) Close

```go
func (s *Subscription) Close() error
```

Close ends the subscription. Frames still queued can be read with Receive until it returns ErrClosed.

#### func (Subscription) Done

```go
func (s *Subscription) Done() <-chan struct{}
```

Done returns a channel closed when the subscription ends.

#### func (Subscription) Dropped

```go
func (s *Subscription) Dropped() uint64
```

Dropped returns the number of frames lost because the queue was full.

#### func (Subscription) Err

```go
func (s *Subscription) Err() error
```

Err returns why the subscription ended, or nil while it is open.

#### func (Subscription) Frames

```go
func (s *Subscription) Frames() <-chan Frame
```

Frames returns the queue as a channel, for use in select statements together with [Subscription.Done](#func-subscription-done). The channel is never closed. A subscription opened [WithXL](#func-withxl) has none (nil): use [Subscription.ReceiveAny](#func-subscription-receiveany).

#### func (Subscription) Receive

```go
func (s *Subscription) Receive(ctx context.Context) (Frame, error)
```

Receive returns the next frame. It returns the context's error when ctx ends first, and, once the queue is empty, ErrClosed after Close or the error that stopped the bus. On a subscription opened [WithXL](#func-withxl) it skips CAN XL frames: use [Subscription.ReceiveAny](#func-subscription-receiveany).

#### func (Subscription) ReceiveAny

```go
func (s *Subscription) ReceiveAny(ctx context.Context, f *Frame, x *XLFrame) (xl bool, err error)
```

ReceiveAny returns the next frame of any kind, in the order the bus received them: a CAN or CAN FD frame in f (xl false) or a CAN XL frame in x (xl true; x.Data is the subscription's copy, owned by the caller afterwards). Without [WithXL](#func-withxl) it is [Subscription.Receive](#func-subscription-receive) into f.

#### func (Subscription) ReceiveXL

```go
func (s *Subscription) ReceiveXL(ctx context.Context) (XLFrame, error)
```

ReceiveXL returns the next CAN XL frame of a subscription opened [WithXL](#func-withxl), like [Subscription.Receive](#func-subscription-receive), skipping CAN and CAN FD frames. Without WithXL it returns ErrUnsupported.

#### func (Subscription) Received

```go
func (s *Subscription) Received() uint64
```

Received returns the number of frames queued so far.

### type Transport

```go
type Transport interface {
	Send(ctx context.Context, f *Frame) error
	Receive(ctx context.Context, f *Frame) error
	Close() error
}
```

Transport is one endpoint on a CAN bus: a SocketCAN socket, a port of a virtual bus, or a future hardware adapter.

Send transmits a frame and Receive waits for the next one; neither retains the frame after it returns. Implementations allow Send from several goroutines at once and one Receive at a time. Both honour the context: a cancelled or expired context ends a blocked call with the context's error. Close ends blocked calls with ErrClosed; later calls return ErrClosed too.

### type XLFlags

```go
type XLFlags uint8
```

XLFlags are the flags of a CAN XL frame (struct canxl\_frame's flags without CANXL\_XLF, which every CAN XL frame carries).

```go
const (
	// XLSEC is the simple extended content bit (security, segmentation).
	XLSEC XLFlags = 0x01
	// XLRRS is the remote request substitution bit (Linux ≥ 6.18 names
	// it; older kernels pass it through as a reserved bit).
	XLRRS XLFlags = 0x02
)
```

CAN XL flags.

#### func (XLFlags) String

```go
func (f XLFlags) String() string
```

String lists the set flags, for example "SEC|RRS".

### type XLFrame

```go
type XLFrame struct {
	// Priority is the 11-bit arbitration priority.
	Priority uint16
	// VCID is the virtual CAN network identifier (0 = none).
	VCID uint8
	// Flags are the frame's flags other than the XL format bit.
	Flags XLFlags
	// SDT is the SDU (service data unit) type of the payload.
	SDT uint8
	// AF is the 32-bit acceptance field.
	AF uint32
	// Data is the payload, 1..2048 bytes.
	Data []byte
	// Timestamp is the receive time reported by the transport, or the
	// zero time.
	Timestamp time.Time
	// Interface names the interface the frame was received on, if known.
	Interface string
	// Echo reports that the frame is the receiving socket's own
	// transmission.
	Echo bool
}
```

XLFrame is one CAN XL frame (ISO 11898-1:2024) with its receive metadata, laid out like Linux's struct canxl\_frame.

Unlike [Frame](#type-frame), the payload is a slice: it holds up to 2048 bytes. Transports copy it; they do not keep it after Send returns.

#### func ParseXLFrame

```go
func ParseXLFrame(s string) (XLFrame, error)
```

ParseXLFrame parses a CAN XL frame in can-utils notation: "\<vcid>\<prio>#\<flags>:\<sdt>:\<af>#\<data>" (five hex digits before the first "#") or "\<prio>#\<flags>:\<sdt>:\<af>#\<data>" (three digits, VCID 0). Data bytes may be separated by dots. The XL format bit 0x80 in the flags is implied, as cansend implies it.

#### func (XLFrame) Clone

```go
func (f *XLFrame) Clone() XLFrame
```

Clone returns a copy of f with its own payload storage.

#### func (XLFrame) String

```go
func (f XLFrame) String() string
```

String formats the frame as can-utils does (cansend, candump): "\<vcid>\<prio>#\<flags>:\<sdt>:\<af>#\<data>" with a two-digit VCID, a three-digit priority and the flags byte including the XL format bit 0x80, for example "00242#80:01:00000000#AABBCC".

#### func (XLFrame) Validate

```go
func (f *XLFrame) Validate() error
```

Validate checks the priority, the payload length and the flags.

### type XLMetrics

```go
type XLMetrics interface {
	// OnXLFrameSent is called after a CAN XL frame was handed to the
	// transport.
	OnXLFrameSent(iface string, x *XLFrame)
	// OnXLFrameReceived is called for every CAN XL frame read from the
	// transport, before filtering by subscriptions.
	OnXLFrameReceived(iface string, x *XLFrame)
}
```

XLMetrics is implemented by [Metrics](#type-metrics) that also observe CAN XL frames. A Bus calls these instead of OnFrameSent and OnFrameReceived for CAN XL frames; Metrics without them see CAN XL frames only in the counters of [Bus.Stats](#func-bus-stats). [NopMetrics](#type-nopmetrics) implements it.

### type XLTransport

```go
type XLTransport interface {
	Transport
	SendXL(ctx context.Context, x *XLFrame) error
	ReceiveAny(ctx context.Context, f *Frame, x *XLFrame) (xl bool, err error)
}
```

XLTransport is implemented by transports that carry CAN XL frames: a SocketCAN socket opened with CAN XL, a virtual bus port. SendXL transmits a CAN XL frame (copying its payload). ReceiveAny waits for the next frame of any kind, a CAN or CAN FD frame in f (xl false) or a CAN XL frame in x (xl true), reusing x.Data's storage; Receive skips CAN XL frames. A [Bus](#type-bus) on an XLTransport receives with ReceiveAny.
